evidence.observation: The plan states: "A caller whose `OUT.semantic_model.*` or `OUT.mapping.*` already exists gets exit 10 (collision) where today's run succeeded." In the code this plan is checked against, the collision band is EXIT_COLLISION = 11 (src/gnd/exits.py:109, "EXIT_COLLISION = 11  # an unmanaged file blocked a write; nothing was destroyed") and the existing ossie export returns it on FileExistsError from publish_new_files (src/gnd/commands/export.py:99-100). Exit 10 is EXIT_DRIFT ("assets stale / missing / modified — doctor's verdict"). The D2 risk the plan documents depends on this exact exit being stated correctly in the changelog and normative text.

concerns.recommendation: Correct the collision exit code to 11 (EXIT_COLLISION) everywhere the plan and later the OB3/OB5 specs and changelog state it, and add a criterion that the new-file collision is asserted against EXIT_COLLISION, not a literal 10.
concerns.title: Plan claims collision exit 10; the codebase's collision band is exit 11

evidence.location: Completion predicates, lines 28-31, vs D2 at line 301
evidence.observation: Predicate 1 states: "`gnd export ossie MODEL --out OUT` behaves exactly as today when no new flag is given and the model's three artifacts each fit in 10 MiB: the three files are byte-identical to the baseline for every model in the export census." But the plan's own proposal D2 (a) (line 301) makes the default write five files, and the plan itself acknowledges the consequence at line 251 ("Default change (D2 a) breaks scripts that rely on three files") and line 301 ("a default run can newly fail (collision, or Rmap refusal) where it succeeded"). Under the proposed ruling, predicate 1 as written is false for no-flag runs and the milestone could not be shown complete; it only holds qualified by --ontology-only, as the plan notes at line 146-147.

concerns.recommendation: Qualify predicate 1 with the D2 ruling, e.g. "under D2 (b), when no new flag is given …; under D2 (a), with --ontology-only", mirroring the existing cross-reference to OB3-C5.
concerns.title: Completion predicate 1 contradicts the proposed D2(a) five-file default

evidence.observation: The plan pins exit 2 for new usage refusals: "`--physical-binding FILE` together with `--ontology-only` is refused as a usage error (exit 2)" (line 149), and OB1-C4 requires the --max-output-bytes argument to be "refused at the CLI boundary when 0, negative, non-integer or above the ceiling (exit 2)". The project's usage band is EXIT_USAGE = 64 (src/gnd/exits.py:46, "EXIT_USAGE = 64") and it is actively returned for usage errors by existing commands (e.g. src/gnd/discover/service.py:491-522, src/gnd/measure/service.py:378). The plan elsewhere treats exit codes as a compatibility contract (exit 3 for refusals, the collision exit in §5), so an unjustified exit 2 for program-level value validation diverges from the house convention and from the exports' own exit vocabulary.

concerns.recommendation: Route these refusals through EXIT_USAGE (64) to match gnd.exits and the other commands, or record an explicit owner-level justification for exit 2 in the plan and carry it into the OB1/OB4 specs, the normative section and the changelog.
concerns.title: New usage-error refusals pin exit 2; GND's usage band is exit 64

response.summary: Reviewed the ossie-relational-bundle plan r1 against the baseline code it names (src/gnd/export/ossie.py, src/gnd/ossie_import.py, src/gnd/commands/export.py, src/gnd/schema/ossie/core-spec.json, src/gnd/schema/ossie/PINNED.json, src/gnd/exits.py, representation-format.md). Most section 1.2 baseline claims verify: ossie:output-size refusal exists and maps to exit 3 (EXIT_ILL_FORMED), ossie_import reads at most MAX_BYTES at lines 66/78, MAX_BYTES and MAX_MODEL_BYTES are 10 MiB, tests/test_ossie_export.py indeed has no output-size coverage, core-spec Dataset has primary_key/unique_keys, Relationship requires name/from/to/from_columns/to_columns, Field requires name/expression, custom_extensions are pervasive, and PINNED.json names only ontology.json plus the core reference. Phase dependencies are acyclic and each decision-gated phase names its ruling (OB1→D3, OB2→D1/D5, OB3→D2/D4/D6, OB4→D7/D8). Three concerns: the plan misstates the existing collision exit code as 10 (code says 11), completion predicate 1 contradicts the proposed D2(a) default, and the new usage-error exit 2 contradicts the project's EXIT_USAGE=64 band.
